findings.title: Weak Menu Highlight
findings.where: Title screen, center menu box around “New Driver”
findings.problem: The selected menu item is indicated only by a 1px neon outline with no fill, making it hard to distinguish from the unselected item when glancing.
findings.why: Players need an immediate visual cue for the current selection; a thin outline lacks weight and can be lost against the busy background, reducing menu usability.
findings.fix: Increase the selected-item border to at least 3px, add a semi-transparent cyan fill (e.g. rgba(0,255,255,0.1)), and darken the unselected item’s background to amplify the contrast.

findings.title: Tagline Contrast Loss
findings.where: Title screen, the line “One car. Sixteen cities. A highway that wants you dead.” directly under the logo
findings.problem: The white tagline text sits directly over bright and mid-tone areas of the background image with no outline or drop shadow, causing legibility issues.
findings.why: Critical flavour text must be readable at first glance; poor contrast against a variable image distracts players and undermines the game’s tone setting.
findings.fix: Add a 1px dark drop shadow (100% opacity, offset 0,2px) to the tagline or place it on a 70%-opacity black rectangle behind the text to guarantee consistent contrast.

findings.title: Unreadable Armor Indicators
findings.where: Arena and Road screens, top-right Condition panel under “Armour”
findings.problem: Each armor slot is depicted as an empty dashed box with no fill or values, making it look like a placeholder rather than a real status indicator.
findings.why: Players must instantly understand how much armor remains on each side; abstract dashed outlines invite confusion and slow decision-making in combat or survival situations.
findings.fix: Replace dashed boxes with filled horizontal bars scaled to current vs max armor, use green for healthy, yellow/red for damage, and overlay numeric percentages (e.g. “Front: 75%”).

findings.title: Flat Radar Display
findings.where: Arena and Road screens, bottom-left “Radar” window
findings.problem: Radar is a dark static circle with a faint grid and no visible sweep or contact blips; the label “Orientation: north-up” is extremely small and low-contrast.
findings.why: Players rely on radar to detect off-screen threats; a non-interactive, poorly labeled radar feels decorative rather than functional and diminishes situational awareness.
findings.fix: Animate a green rotating sweep line at 2 seconds per revolution, draw incoming object blips in bright yellow, and increase the orientation label to 12px semi-bold white for readability.

findings.title: Constructor UI Lacks Focus
findings.where: Vehicle constructor screen, left-side list of fields and values
findings.problem: All text rows (Name, Body, Chassis, Weapon slots) are identical in weight and color, and the currently editable row has no distinct background or cursor indicator.
findings.why: Without clear input affordance or hierarchy, players may not realize where to enter data or how to navigate the list, leading to onboarding friction.
findings.fix: Highlight the active row with a 4px tall cyan bar behind the text, change editable fields to light-grey backgrounds, and bold category headers (Body, Suspension, Tires) to create a visual hierarchy.
